posts.text:
I don’t think the Trop is “so bad.”

But it is not in the same class as Fenway, PNC, Wrigley, SanFran or Camden Yards, as well as others like Petco, old Yankee Stadium, etc.


Brandon Johnson (@brxAgain)

Why do you think the Trop is so bad? It's what Florida needs - nice and cool, protected from Thunderstorms, and seats plenty while the population keeps growing..



— https://nitter.net/brxAgain/status/2038088957850730958#m

No way.  When you walk up and see the Green Monster it is a unique experience.  

Not everything needs to be a modern luxury.  There is a charm to the place especially given all the history there.


SealedGain (@SealedGain)

Fenway looks nice on TV, but actually sucks to attend



— https://nitter.net/SealedGain/status/2038018134762811577#m

It’d be hard to beat having the Polo Grounds, Yankee Stadium and Ebbets Field all in the same city.


AlbatrossHunter (@ZebbaWax)

Agreed, Ron. The old one was a dangerous environment for the road team. Especially near the bleachers in a close game. On a side note it would be cool to travel back in time and see a game at the Polo Grounds.



— https://nitter.net/ZebbaWax/status/2038066400019743196#m

I haven’t been since my Navy days but it is definitely a great park.


Tim K 🇺🇸 (@Tim_Koerner)

Petco in San Diego is awesome as well.



— https://nitter.net/Tim_Koerner/status/2038063301825876234#m

Yes I like it.  I also like Milwaukee in the summer.


Illinois Conservative🇺🇸🇻🇦 (@IL4Liberty)

Ever been to American Family field (aka Miller Park & County Stadium)? 

I’ll be there tomorrow. Awesome place.



— https://nitter.net/IL4Liberty/status/2038057584167473335#m

Uh, I don’t think anyone is claiming the Trop is a great ballpark…


Joey (@JosephH11112238)

If you don’t like the new Yankee stadium I’d love your thoughts on the trop which looks like the most depressing place ever to watch a game



— https://nitter.net/JosephH11112238/status/2038068501890355663#m

Not the new Yankee Stadium.  Just felt very corporate to me compared to the old (amazing) one, which I loved.


GallopingGhost (@GallopingGhos11)

No Yankee Stadium?



— https://nitter.net/GallopingGhos11/status/2038060599704223872#m

I’d probably have Camden Yards in my top 5 along with Wrigley, PNC, Fenway and Oracle.  

Note that I haven’t been to Dodger Stadium.


Mark (@MarkSmith7890)

Camden Yards?



— https://nitter.net/MarkSmith7890/status/2038047600520142913#m

Adjusting $32 billion for population growth and inflation (which is appropriate to do) does not get you even close to $60 billion.


Will (@willixm4america)

Does that not happen because of the sudden sharp growth Florida has seen in the past 10 years? More homes more tax revenue more demand for services etc



— https://nitter.net/willixm4america/status/2038019210677195002#m

Top 5


George Adams (@george_adams21)

Where would you have Wrigley Field ranked?



— https://nitter.net/george_adams21/status/2038020683880358132#m

It was the original retro park — first time I went decades ago I was blown away.


Brian Jackson (@briancjackson)

Camden Yards has its own charm.  It should rate at least top five.



— https://nitter.net/briancjackson/status/2038018599734878405#m

Yes — unless you have 86 Fleer basketball in unopened boxes.


Ricky Spanish (@jibbs_mcge76431)

as someone whose sorting thru my dads 80's sealed boxes, nothing is worse than the junk wax era.



— https://nitter.net/jibbs_mcge76431/status/2038009775774978363#m

Ugh.  That’s terrible to see especially with such a great player.


Warchant.com (@Warchant)

Gut-wrenching scene at Howser as FSU star Myles Bailey is carted off following a lower leg injury on a slide into second





— https://nitter.net/Warchant/status/2038002418797998512#m

Score overproduced them (like all brands from that era were doing).


WildBillNC (@WildBillNC1978)

As an Auburn man I 100 percent agree with you, I only wish 1990 Score didn't mass produce them. I have about 25 in my collection that I have held onto since I pulled them from packs as a 12-year-old kid. 😀



— https://nitter.net/WildBillNC1978/status/2037970660165579116#m

89 UD Griffey was my favorite rookie card of the 80s.  Too bad UD cranked the printing presses and overproduced them.


Major Swagger 🔥 (@Maj0rSwagger)

Agreed 

Couple others I liked were:

‘89 Upper Deck Griffey 
‘91 Upper Deck Jordan in Sox uniform







— https://nitter.net/Maj0rSwagger/status/2037994029133275136#m

No — I’d put Fenway and PNC above Petco.


TodayInSports (@TodayInSportsCo)

Do you agree?   ⚾️





— https://nitter.net/TodayInSportsCo/status/2037971487324307648#m

The old radar guns were reliable; they just clocked the speed closer to the plate.  Today’s guns pick it up closer to the pitcher’s hand.


Shane Funk (@TheBigFunk)

They say he threw harder than that, old radar guns werent near as reliable. Same with Nolan Ryan, wish we had a radar gun for Walter Johnson



— https://nitter.net/TheBigFunk/status/2037976466030301300#m

The reality is that local governments taxed $32 billion on property in 2019.  Today, that has ballooned to $60 billion.  

If no relief is enacted, that number is projected to be $84 billion by the beginning of next decade — almost a tripling of the tax revenue in a little more than 10 years.

Not sustainable for our homesteaded taxpaying Floridians!


Blaise Ingoglia (@GovGoneWild)

This article is inaccurate. 

Here’s why: 

1) The proposal is to get rid of property taxes on HOMESTEADED proper

That is some serious smoke!


Baseball’s Greatest Moments (@BBGreatMoments)

Bob Feller's fastball is clocked at 98.6 mph using a United States Army ordinance device.

Video
  





— https://nitter.net/BBGreatMoments/status/2037956694118981752#m

That Score card was one of the best of all-time.


BaseballHistoryNut (@nut_history)

Bo Jackson in arguably the greatest sports cards photos of all time.





— https://nitter.net/nut_history/status/2037923201750102490#m
